**Best move:** Rxd5+

**Main line:** Rxd5+ Kg6 Rd6+ Kh7 Rd7+ Kh8 Rxd1

**Motif:** Skewer

**Explanation:**
Your rook captures the undefended bishop with check, forcing the king up the board. The knight on d1 remains trapped and defenseless the whole time—the rook skewers the king and knight, meaning it pins the king because moving it would lose the knight. You then systematically drive the king to the corner and collect the knight for free, winning +3 material decisively.

**Lesson:** When your opponent leaves two pieces on the same line, check if one is pinned to the king. A skewer is a "reversed pin"—attacking the more valuable piece first and the defender second. Look for ways to give check that line up your opponent's pieces.
